title: Expected Value Alignment for Generative Reward Modeling in Formal Mathematics Verification
abstract: arXiv:2606.01160v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used with formal interactive theorem provers such as Lean 4. Scaling these systems with reinforcement learning or search methods requires process reward models (PRMs) that can evaluate intermediate reasoning steps. Existing reward-model designs expose a practical trade-off. Value-head models provide continuous scores but modify the generative model interface, while generative reward models preserve textual rationales but are poorly matched to continuous floating-point regression because numeric values are split across tokens. We introduce Expected Value Alignment (EVA), a reward-modeling procedure that keeps the surface output discrete while extracting continuous scores from the model's token distribution. translated_title: 形式数学验证中生成式奖励建模的期望值对齐
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）越来越多地与Lean 4等正式交互式定理证明器结合使用。通过强化学习或搜索方法扩展这些系统需要能够评估中间推理步骤的过程奖励模型（PRMs）。现有的奖励模型设计暴露了一个实际权衡：值头模型提供连续分数但修改了生成模型的接口，而生成式奖励模型保留了文本推理但难以匹配连续浮点回归，因为数值被分割到多个令牌中。我们引入了期望值对齐（EVA），这是一种奖励建模程序，它保持表面输出为离散形式，同时从模型的令牌分布中提取连续分数。模型以结构化JSON格式输出整数分数，EVA通过计算相应锚定令牌的对数几率上的期望值来计算连续分数。训练结合了...
tldr: 本文提出EVA方法，通过从令牌分布中提取期望值，在保持生成式奖励模型离散输出的同时获得连续分数，解决了形式数学验证中奖励建模的数值回归难题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces EVA, which extracts expected values from token distributions to obtain continuous scores while keeping generative reward models' discrete output, addressing the numeric regression challenge in formal math verification.
